hero.kicker: Lawn care, landscaping and snow removal in Linden, MI
hero.title: A mill town on **soft ground.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows, cleans up, rebuilds beds and plows in Linden, the small city that grew up around the mill on the Shiawassee River. Older lots near downtown, newer ones toward the edges, and low, wet ground in between.

about.title: Built around a mill pond, on ground that **holds water.**
body: Linden began as a village in 1871 around the corner of Bridge and Broad, with buildings going back to 1840, and became a city in 1988. About 4,000 people live here. The old mill building stands on the bank of the Shiawassee River with the Mill Pond park across the water, and the city keeps a historic district downtown.

The land is low. This is country of marsh, swamp and old marl bottom lakes, and the USDA soil survey shows it: rolling, well drained Wawasee loam and sandy Boyer soils on the higher ground, some on slopes of 6 to 12 percent, and very poorly drained Carlisle and Linwood muck under about one sample point in six across the city.
Step past the city limits and you are in Fenton Township, where the county plows the roads and the houses spread out.

points.title: Low spots that stay wet
points.body: Muck holds water long after a rain. A lawn on it can look fine and still rut under a mower, so we read the ground on mowing day and work around a soft corner instead of tracking it up. Low spots are also where a bed planted with the wrong things gives up first.

points.title: Slopes on the high ground
points.body: The rolling Wawasee loam sheds water and dries out first, and bare soil on a slope washes away. A high cut keeps the grass thicker there, and a block or boulder border can hold a bed that keeps sliding toward the walk. That is [landscaping](/landscaping-linden-mi/) work.

points.title: Yard waste runs into December
points.body: Priority Waste picks up city yard waste on Wednesdays from April 1 into early December; in 2026 the last pickup is December 2. Leaves go in paper bags or marked containers of up to 35 gallons, each under 50 pounds, and branches get bundled in lengths of 4 feet or less.

points.title: Cars off the street all winter
points.body: The city's fall newsletter lists no on-street parking from November 1 to March 31, starting at 2:30 in the morning. Check with City Hall for the exact hours. Streets without parked cars are streets the DPW can plow curb to curb.

points.title: Ask before you burn
points.body: A burn permit is one of the city's most requested forms. If you are thinking about burning a leaf pile, check the permit terms with City Hall first, or skip the smoke and let us haul the leaves off in a [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-linden-mi/).

logistics.title: Booked on a set day, the same as our home town.
body: Linden is about 25 minutes from our shop on Embury Road, so yards here are booked on a set day each week instead of squeezed in between other stops. Rob drives out for the estimate, walks the yard with you, suggests what it needs and gives you a price.

In the city, the public works crew clears more than 17 miles of streets, some of them dirt. Out in Fenton Township the Genesee County Road Commission plows, with subdivision streets last. Either way, our part is your drive and walks, plowed by our own trucks and treated where people walk.

faq.q: Do you work in Linden, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes works in the City of Linden and the Fenton Township lots around it. We do weekly [lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing-linden-mi/), [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-linden-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-linden-mi/) and [snow removal](/snow-removal-linden-mi/), and Rob gives free estimates. Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040).

faq.q: When is the last yard waste pickup of the year in Linden?
faq.a: In 2026 it is Wednesday, December 2, the last of the weekly compost pickups by Priority Waste that started April 1. Yard waste goes in paper bags or marked containers up to 35 gallons, each under 50 pounds. The dates change each year, so check the city's trash page for the current calendar.

faq.q: Who clears the streets in Linden?
faq.a: The city's Department of Public Works, a five person staff that also looks after water, sewer, parks and city buildings, maintains more than 17 miles of city streets, including snow and ice removal and grading the dirt roads. Roads outside the city in Fenton Township are plowed by the Genesee County Road Commission.

faq.q: Do you take care of the wet, low lots around town?
faq.a: Yes. Much of the city is lowland, and the soil survey shows very poorly drained muck in the low spots. We mow those lawns when the ground will carry a mower, trim the soft edges by hand when it will not, and can rebuild a bed that keeps drowning with plants and a layout that suit wet ground.
